facts.text: A Pacific bluefin tuna can grow to 4 meters long and weigh up to 500 kilograms.
Bluefin swim into the waters east of Taiwan to spawn in May and June, and Taiwan's bluefin season usually runs from April to June.
Pacific bluefin spawn in waters between central Japan and the northern Philippines and in the Sea of Japan.
To win the title of Pingtung's first bluefin of the season, a Taiwan-registered boat must be the first to bring a bluefin of at least 175 kilograms back to a local port.
In April 2026 the season's first bluefin, a 190-kilogram fish, sold at the Donggang fish market for a record NT$10,600 per kilogram, or about NT$2.014 million in all.
The 2026 price per kilogram was NT$300 higher than the price paid for the first bluefin a year earlier.
By June 2025, the bluefin tuna festival held each season at Donggang had been running for 25 years.
By 9 May 2003, Donggang fishermen had caught 695 bluefin, compared with 1,500 by the same date a year earlier.
Overfishing in the late 1990s and the 2000s cut the Pacific bluefin spawning stock to about 2 percent of its unfished level in 2009 to 2012.
In 2011, members of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission agreed to reduce catches of both young and adult bluefin; the eastern Pacific commission followed in 2012.
The two commissions set a goal of rebuilding the spawning stock to at least 20 percent of its unfished level by 2034; it reached that goal in 2021.
According to the 2024 assessment, the spawning stock had reached 23.2 percent of its unfished level in 2022.
In June 2024, more than 90 percent of Taiwan's national bluefin quota had been used by 9 June, so the Fisheries Agency banned bluefin fishing from 12 June.
Taiwan's fishery statistics list tuna longline catches under two groups: distant-water fisheries and offshore fisheries.
Taiwan's distant-water tuna longline boats caught 1,482 tonnes of Pacific bluefin in 2003 and 130 tonnes in 2012, a drop of about 91 percent.
Taiwan's offshore tuna longline boats caught 826 tonnes of Pacific bluefin in 2003 and 80 tonnes in 2012, a drop of about 90 percent.
In 2023, Taiwan's offshore longline boats caught 1,003 tonnes of Pacific bluefin, more than they caught in 2003; the distant-water boats caught 1,114 tonnes.
